questions.problem:
The probability distribution of the random variable $X$ is given below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=7,$ calculate $\text{Var}[5X].$ 

| $x$ | $5$ | $6$ | $9$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{2}{5}$ | $\frac{2}{5}$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constant $a,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[aX]={a}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X].
$$

In our case, $a=5.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[5X] & ={5}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =25\cdot \text{Var}[X].\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the variance of $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

Additionally, we're given that $\text{E}[X]=7.$ 

We start by computing $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={5}^{2}\cdot f(5)+{6}^{2}\cdot f(6)+{9}^{2}\cdot f(9) \\  & =25(\frac{1}{5})+36(\frac{2}{5})+81(\frac{2}{5}) \\  & =\frac{259}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{259}{5}-{7}^{2} \\  & =\frac{259}{5}-49 \\  & =\frac{14}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[5X] & =25\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =25\cdot \frac{14}{5} \\  & =14\cdot 5 \\  & =70.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The probability distribution of the random variable $X$ is given below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{9}{2},$ calculate $\text{Var}[3-\frac{1}{2}X].$ 

| $x$ | $0$ | $3$ | $6$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{5}{8}$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constants $a$ and $b,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[aX+b]={a}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X].
$$

In our case, $a=-\frac{1}{2}$ and $b=3.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[3-\frac{1}{2}X] & ={(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \text{Var}[X].\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the variance of $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

Additionally, we're given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{9}{2}.$ 

We start by computing $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={0}^{2}\cdot f(0)+{3}^{2}\cdot f(3)+{6}^{2}\cdot f(6) \\  & =9\cdot \frac{1}{4}+36\cdot \frac{5}{8} \\  & =\frac{99}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{99}{4}-{(\frac{9}{2})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[3-\frac{1}{2}X] & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{9}{2} \\  & =\frac{9}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The probability distribution of the random variable $X$ is given below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=2,$ calculate $\text{Var}[\sqrt{3}X-5].$ 

| $x$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constants $a$ and $b,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[aX+b]={a}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X].
$$

In our case, $a=\sqrt{3}$ and $b=-5.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\sqrt{3}X-5] & ={\sqrt{3}}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =3\cdot \text{Var}[X].\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the variance of $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

Additionally, we're given that $\text{E}[X]=2.$ 

We start by computing $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={0}^{2}\cdot f(0)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{4}^{2}\cdot f(4) \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{3}+16\cdot \frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{20}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{20}{3}-{2}^{2} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\sqrt{3}X-5] & =3\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =3\cdot \frac{8}{3} \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
